figures.finding: The statutory minimum for screen performers is the Broadcasting, Recorded Entertainment and Cinemas Award 2020 (MA000091), a modern award made and varied by the Fair Work Commission; its artist rates were last varied from the first full pay period on or after 1 July 2026.

figures.finding: From 1 July 2026 a screen performer's award minimum is A$341.98 a day on a feature film (A$359.30 for a Class 2 performer, one with five years' professional work) and A$293.13 a day on other content (A$307.99 Class 2); A$1,221.10 a week (A$1,283.10 Class 2); a feature performer with two lines or fewer is paid A$53.87 an hour (4-hour minimum), an extra A$268.61 a day; the day is 8 hours, the week 38, juveniles 50%.

figures.finding: From 1 July 2026 a stage actor's award minimum is A$1,221.10 a week for up to 38 hours and 8 full-length performances (Performer Category 1 Grade 1, under three years' experience) or A$1,283.10 (Grade 2); a casual is paid 16.7% of the weekly rate plus 25% per performance and A$53.72 for the first rehearsal hour; children under 15 off tour 45%.

figures.finding: Most film and television work has historically been in New South Wales (Sydney), around half of drama production spending since 1995/96 (47% in 2023/24), though Queensland led in 2024/25 with 34% to New South Wales's 31% and Victoria's 27%.
figures.applies: Australia, drama production expenditure (local and foreign), Screen Australia Drama Report.

sources.said: Historically has accounted for around half of all drama production spending since 1995/96. In 2023/24, expenditure was $799 million, which accounted for 47% of total spend in Australia
The proportion of spend for states and territories was 34% in Queensland, 31% in New South Wales, 27% in Victoria, 3% in South Australia, 3% in Western Australia
